Impact Assessment
Taken as a whole, the environmental impact from the alternative specific projects not chosen for the Community Development Block Grant program would not have a significant adverse environmental impact. Certain projects such as the Olinder sidewalk improvements, the Gardner Street improvements, and the Campus demolition and parking lot construction would have minor and temporary effects upon local air quality, ambient noise and solid waste disposal. The nature of such impact, have previously been examined. They are not significant. Other proposed but rejected projects would have a positive and long-lasting impact on the social environment; i.e., the Housing Service Center projects, neighborhood rehabilitation in Alviso, Alma, Anne Darling, and the various park and recreation projects. Many of these projects would also involve minor short-term physical impacts, but these would be off-set by the positive human impact. The positive impacts derived from these alternative projects would neither be greater or lesser than the impacts of the selected projects.
B. LIMITATION OF PROJECTS TO CERTAIN CATEGORIES
Neighborhood Housing Rehabilitation
This alternative would concentrate all CDBG funds in the physical rehabilitation of residential area, both those chosen as CNRA's and in those areas not selected, but proposed. The general nature of this alternative would be like that rehabilitation planned for the Mayfair, Gardner, Northside, Olinder and Campus areas, but would affect more dwelling units.
The rehabilitation alternative allows the direct problems associated with chronic housing deficiencies to be singled out for special attention without a civersion of funds to other non-housing uses.
